summaries.sq1: At low to medium request volumes, hosted LLM APIs provide a lower total cost of ownership than self-hosting [ev3]. Rented cloud GPUs for inference cost between $1.50 and $4.00 per hour ($1,100 to $2,900 per month for 24/7 uptime) before storage, networking, and monitoring [ev5]. The direct compute break-even point for self-hosting is estimated between 1 to 3 billion tokens per month [ev6]. When including engineering labor required for setup, maintenance, monitoring, and scaling, the labor cost for self-hosting outweighs compute savings until volume reaches several billion tokens per month [ev2].

summaries.sq2: Keeping a self-hosted open-weight model reliable in production requires between 0.25 and 0.5 of a full-time engineer on an ongoing basis according to TCO models for small engineering teams [ev1]. Open issues: Only one source provided specific engineering allocation figures; details on exact DevOps toolchains or infrastructure scaling metrics for small startups remain limited in the retrieved evidence.

agreements: Self-hosting open-weight models requires ongoing engineering maintenance for monitoring, scaling, and upgrades [ev1, ev9].
The break-even point where self-hosting becomes more cost-effective than hosted APIs is around several billion tokens per month [ev2, ev3, ev6, ev8].

report.title: Cloud LLM APIs vs Self-Hosting Open-Source Models for a 5-Person Startup
report.executive_summary: A 5-person startup should use cloud LLM APIs rather than self-hosting unless its token volume exceeds several billion per month. Below this threshold, hosted APIs provide a lower total cost of ownership because the engineering labor required to maintain self-hosted models outweighs potential compute savings. This decision depends heavily on monthly token volume and the opportunity cost of engineering headcount.

findings.statement: Keeping a self-hosted open-weight model reliable in production requires 0.25 to 0.5 of a full-time engineer for ongoing maintenance, patching, and monitoring.
At typical startup engineering costs, the labor required for self-hosting outweighs compute savings until volume reaches several billion tokens per month.
On-demand rentals for a single inference-class GPU range from $1.50 to $4.00 per hour, translating to roughly $1,100 to $2,900 per month around the clock.
The break-even point for self-hosting falls between 1 and 3 billion tokens per month, below which GPUs sit idle and effective costs exceed API pricing.
Initial setup for serving, autoscaling, and monitoring takes about three weeks of engineering time before ongoing maintenance begins.

limitations: The risk analysis subquestion failed to gather evidence, leaving data privacy, security, and compliance risks unaddressed.
Evidence sources do not cover specialized hardware optimizations or multi-region high availability costs.
report.recommendation: Use cloud LLM APIs for all product features until monthly token volume consistently exceeds 1 to 3 billion tokens; revisit self-hosting only when growth justifies dedicating 0.25 to 0.5 of an engineer to infrastructure maintenance.
